test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate direct form of the given sentence.**

She says that she would like to be an ambassador to a foreign country when she grows up.

options.text: She told, “I like to be an ambassador to a foreign country when I grow up.”
She says, “I would like to be an ambassador to a foreign country when I grow up.”
She says, “She likes to be an ambassador to a foreign country when she grows up.”
She said, “She would like to be an ambassador to a foreign country when she grew up.”

solution:
The correct answer is- 'She says, “I would like to be an ambassador to a foreign country when I grow up.”'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To change the sentence to a direct speech we need to follow the following steps:

 
 
• In the given sentence, the **reporting speech **is in the *present tense*.
 
• We know that when the **reporting speech **is in the *present tense *there is **no change **in the tense of the **reported speech**.
 
• The **conjunction **'*that*' should be replaced by an **inverted comma**, enclosing the **reported speech**.
 
• The pronoun ***she* **will change to ***I***. 
 
 
 
• Thus according to the given steps, *option 2 *is the correct answer.

And the correct sentence is: *She says, “I would like to be an ambassador to a foreign country when I grow up.”*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** ​

 
• Here are some **rules **that should be followed while converting an **indirect speech **to **direct speech**:

 
 
• Use the **reporting verb **such as (*say, said to*) in its correct tense.
 
• Put a **comma **before the statement and the **first letter **of the statement should be in **capital letter**.
 
• **Insert ***question marks*, *quotation marks*, *exclamation marks *and *full stop*, based on the **mood **of the sentence.
 
• Remove the **conjunctions **like (*that, to, if *or *whether*) wherever necessary.
 
• Where the **reporting verb **is in the **past tense **in indirect, change it to **present tense **in the direct speech.
 
• Change the **past perfect tense **either into **present perfect tense **or **past indefinite tense**, as necessary.
